Small action: Accept one sincere compliment without dismissing your effort. You can acknowledge others without erasing your contribution.
Example words: Thank you. I put a lot of care into it.
Reflection: What did they appreciate? What effort or skill can I acknowledge in myself?

Small action: Ask one clear and respectful question without an unnecessary apology. Respect the other person's time; apologize appropriately for an actual mistake.
Example words: Could you clarify the deadline? / Is now a good time for a quick question?
Reflection: Did my question need an apology or simply a polite opening?

Small action: Name a real commitment or capacity limit. Consider responsibilities and the effect on others before setting a reasonable limit on a non-urgent request.
Example words: I already have plans tonight so I can't help this time. / I can look at it tomorrow if that works.
Reflection: What makes this limit fair? Am I protecting a real need while communicating respectfully?

Small action: Name guilt or discomfort without treating it as proof of wrongdoing. Check commitments and avoidable harm; consider specific legitimate feedback and repair or adjust if warranted.
Example words: I understand you're disappointed. I still can't today.
Reflection: What am I feeling? What evidence supports my decision and what feedback should I consider?

Small action: Write down one moment of self-respect from the week. Notice what was difficult and choose one small action to repeat.
Example words: One thing I handled with self-respect was ____. Next week I will practice ____.
Reflection: Which action helped me stay both kind and clear? What small action will I repeat?
